title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## TacPAC: Real-Time Tactile Action Correction

### The Breakthrough
TacPAC predicts tactile contact images, caches them, and uses a tactile expert to compare live observations and issue a single‑pass correction that is 20.7× cheaper than replanning, raising manipulation success from 22% to 64% across five real‑robot tasks.

### The Caveats
TacPAC is only benchmarked against an unnamed vision‑only baseline and never compared to existing tactile‑based correction methods.

## FIRE-LIVWO: Robust Multimodal Odometry for Underground

### The Breakthrough
The system fuses 4D mmWave radar, LiDAR, visual features, and wheel odometry in an iterated error‑state Kalman filter with Doppler constraints, achieving an average localization error of 5.677 cm in underground coal‑mine tests, outperforming unspecified baselines.

### The Caveats
The claimed error improvement is against unspecified baselines, leaving its robustness unverified.

## Conditional Visual Grounding in Imitation Policies

### The Breakthrough
By adding distractor augmentation, phase‑dependent attention regularization, and appearance‑based visual prompting to the ACT transformer policy, the authors improve target selection robustness on simulated tasks and a real UR3e robot.

### The Caveats
Evaluation is only against the unaugmented ACT policy with no comparison to established visuomotor baselines.

## Humanoid Robot Prototype for Multimodal HRI

### The Breakthrough
A 12‑DOF dual‑arm humanoid with a Jetson runs MediaPipe Pose+LSTM gesture classification, YOLO‑based 3D object detection, and speech‑to‑text plus LLM parsing, achieving 96% gesture, 92% speech accuracy and sub‑2 cm manipulation error with >90% task success.

### The Caveats
Reported accuracies are not benchmarked against existing humanoid platforms.

## visloc-rs: Fast Pure‑Rust Visual SLAM

### The Breakthrough
The Rust library implements feature extraction, matching, and a memory‑bounded mapper, delivering a 3.46× speedup over COLMAP on a 1,200‑image dataset and up to 66.7% lower RMSE, while using ≤3.32 GiB RAM and registering 99.88% of cameras.

### The Caveats
Speedup and error reductions are demonstrated only against COLMAP, with no other SLAM comparisons.

## quackd: LLM‑Powered Brain Daemon for Small Robots

### The Breakthrough
quackd translates natural‑language goals into robot‑specific skill sequences via LLMs, enforces a .duck safety contract, supports eight robot bodies, runs on a bundled simulator, and can offload reasoning to cloud or local LLM servers without API keys.

### The Caveats
The hardware‑ready claim is unverified; the repo provides only a simulated demo with no real‑robot experiments.

## TAMU‑Robomasters Taproot Aimbots Rewrite

### The Breakthrough
The repository rewrites the 2021 Aimbots platform using modern C++20 and FreeRTOS within the Taproot framework, offering a modular embedded stack and build documentation for competition robots.

### The Caveats
No performance evaluation or baseline comparison is provided, so improvement is unclear.

## HexBOTs: Cellular Automaton of Robotic Lawn‑Mowers

### The Breakthrough
HexBOTs is a browser‑based deterministic cellular automaton where each cell is a robot with a genome‑based rule set, enabling an astronomically large space of robot types without runtime randomness and instant user experimentation.

### The Caveats
The demo lacks quantitative or comparative evaluation of its emergent patterns.

## China Readies Humanoid Robots for Combat

### The Breakthrough
A report claims China is developing humanoid robots intended for combat tasks, suggesting advances in mobility, autonomy, and potential weapon integration.

### The Caveats
The claim lacks concrete evidence, trials, or independent verification.

### Priority
TacPAC offers a concrete, real‑world tactile correction that dramatically boosts manipulation success and provides open‑source code and data for immediate use.

### One action
Clone the TacPAC repository, examine the released dataset, and prototype tactile‑feedback correction in your own manipulation pipeline.
